t.1.107.1: Then, O Janamejaya, a hundred sons were born to Dhṛtarāṣṭra by Gāndhārī, and one more beyond the hundred by a Vaiśya woman.
t.1.107.2: To Pāṇḍu, in Kuntī and in Mādrī, five sons, great chariot-warriors, were born from the gods, for the continuation of the lineage.
t.1.107.3: Janamejaya said: How were a hundred sons born to Gāndhārī, O best of the twice-born, and in how much time? And what was the full span of their lives?
t.1.107.4: And how was that one son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra born of a vaiśyā woman? And how did Dhṛtarāṣṭra pass over Gāndhārī, his worthy wife, who walked in dharma and conducted herself in devoted compliance with him?
t.1.107.5: And how, when Pāṇḍu had been cursed by that great-souled one, were five sons, great chariot-warriors, born to him from the gods?
t.1.107.6: O learned one, rich in austerities, tell me this in detail, just as it happened; I find no satiety while the tale of my kinsmen is being told.
t.1.107.7: Gāndhārī pleased Dvaipāyana, who had arrived exhausted by hunger and fatigue, and Vyāsa granted her a boon.
t.1.107.9: For two years Gāndhārī, still without offspring, carried that conceived embryo; then grief came over her.
t.1.107.8: She chose for herself a hundred sons equal to her husband. Then, in due time, she conceived an embryo by Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
t.1.107.10: Having heard that a son had been born to Kuntī, equal in splendor to the rising sun, and perceiving the steadiness of her own womb, she brooded over it.
t.1.107.11: Then Gāndhārī, faint with grief, unknown to Dhṛtarāṣṭra and with great effort, caused the contents of her womb to fall.
t.1.107.12: Then a lump of flesh was born, compact like a ball of iron; she began to cast out that mass which had been borne in her womb for two years.
t.1.107.13: Then Dvaipāyana, having come to know of it, came there in haste, and he, the best of those who murmur prayers, beheld that lump of flesh.
t.1.107.14: Then he said to the daughter of Subala, "What is this that you intend to do?" And she truthfully told the supreme seer what she had in mind.
t.1.107.15: Having heard that Kuntī's eldest son had been born, radiant as the sun, I, in the utmost anguish, caused this womb of mine to fall.
t.1.107.16: Long ago, it is said, a hundred sons were granted to me by you; yet this lump of flesh has been born to me in place of a hundred sons.
t.1.107.18: Let a hundred pots filled with ghee be prepared at once, and sprinkle this ball of flesh with cool water.
t.1.107.17: So it is, Saubaleyī; this can never be otherwise. Never before have I spoken falsely, not even in idle talk, so how could this be otherwise?
t.1.107.20: Then, O lord of the people, O king, from that lump of flesh a full hundred and one came forth in due order, one after another, with the passing of time.
t.1.107.19: Then that ball of flesh, as it was being sprinkled, became a hundredfold, separate embryos, each the size of the joint of a thumb.
t.1.107.21: Then he placed those embryos in those pots, set them in well-guarded places, and thereafter arranged for their protection.
t.1.107.22: And the blessed one further instructed Saubalī: "After this much time has passed, these pots are to be broken open."
t.1.107.23: Having spoken thus and having made the arrangements accordingly, the wise and blessed Vyāsa went to the Himavant, that mass of rock, to practise austerities.
t.1.107.25: As soon as that son was born, Dhṛtarāṣṭra assembled many brahmins, as well as Bhīṣma and Vidura, and spoke these words.
t.1.107.24: In this sequence King Duryodhana was born among them, but by the reckoning of birth King Yudhiṣṭhira was the eldest.
t.1.107.26: Yudhiṣṭhira, the king's son, the eldest of us and the increaser of our lineage, has obtained the kingdom by his own merits; we have nothing to say against him.
t.1.107.27: But this one, born next after him, will he too become king? Tell me this truly, what will surely come to pass in this matter.
t.1.107.28: At the close of these words, O Bhārata, in all directions fearsome flesh-eating creatures cried out, and so did jackals, heralds of ill omen.
t.1.107.29: Having observed all those dreadful omens on every side, the brāhmaṇas, O king, and the greatly wise Vidura spoke.
t.1.107.31: Let there be a hundred sons less one for you, O lord of the earth; by the one, secure the welfare of the world and of the family.
t.1.107.30: Clearly this son of yours will become the destroyer of the family. Peace lies in abandoning him, but in nurturing him there is great calamity.
t.1.107.32: For the sake of the family one should abandon a single person; for the sake of the village one should abandon the family; for the sake of the country, the village; and for the sake of oneself one should abandon the earth.
t.1.107.33: Though he was told this by Vidura and by all those excellent brahmins, the king, filled with love for his son, did not do so.
t.1.107.34: Then, O king, within the space of a single month all the hundred sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra were born, and one daughter besides, over and above the hundred.
t.1.107.35: While Gāndhārī was suffering with her swelling belly, a Vaiśya woman, it is said, waited upon the mighty-armed Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
t.1.107.37: Thus were born to the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra a hundred sons, heroes and great chariot-warriors, and also one daughter, Duḥśalā.
t.1.107.36: In that year, O king, the illustrious and wise Yuyutsu, a karaṇa, was then born of Dhṛtarāṣṭra in her, O lord of men.
